https://github.com/audreyt/pugs/blob/mas.who: Audrey Tang (then Autrijus), creator of Pugs, and the Pugs developers
https://github.com/audreyt/pugs/blob/mas.says: Lists chained comparisons and junctions in the first release, 6.0.0, then multimethod dispatch and parameter binding within a week, PGE-based rules in 6.2.3, and reduction, hyper forms and gather/take in 6.2.4.

https://raku.github.io/CCR/Remaster/Patr.who: Patrick Michaud, lead developer of the Perl 6 compiler on Parrot
https://raku.github.io/CCR/Remaster/Patr.where: Michaud's blog post on the compiler's new name, as copied in the CCR Remaster collection (which rewrites Perl 6 as Raku)
https://raku.github.io/CCR/Remaster/Patr.says: Announces Rakudo Perl, Rakudo for short, as the name of the Perl 6 compiler on Parrot, quoting Damian Conway's proposal, and reserves Perl 6 for the language specification itself.

https://github.com/rakudo/rakudo/blob/ma.says: Announces that release 197 switches Rakudo to its RakuAST-based grammar and actions by default, calls this a milestone on the way to language level 6.e, and says 6.e itself will come later.

https://www.perl.com/pub/2001/10/02/apoc.says: Defines binary ~~ as a logical exclusive-or operator and gives hyper operators a caret prefix, so @a ^* @b multiplies two arrays element by element.

https://www.perl.com/pub/2002/01/15/apo4.says: Adopts given and when in place of switch and case, and presents its table of match rules as the definition of how Perl 6's =~ operator behaves.

https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.where: perl6-language mailing list, Re: perl6 operator precedence table (msg11632)
https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.says: Argues smart matching merits a weightier operator and suggests ~~ for it, while also floating === and several other spellings and saying that for now he prefers the English word like.

https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.who: Piers Cawley, writer of the weekly Perl 6 Summary
https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.where: perl6-language mailing list, Perl 6 Summary for the week ending 27 Oct 2002 (msg12116)
https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.says: Reports, among operator choices that look settled, that ~~ replaces =~ to avoid confusion with the string-append ~=, while !~ stays as it was.

https://www.perl.com/pub/2003/03/07/apoc.says: Uses ~~ for smart matching, in an example that tests the caller's context through the want function.

https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.where: Raku/old-design-docs commit b22582e (Pugs svn r13527), Functions.pod
https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.says: Adds a generalized pick to the built-in functions document, with signatures that take a Whatever argument so that passing a star returns every element in random order.

https://github.com/rakudo/rakudo/blob/ma.says: Notes in the 2009-04 release that a method call on the Whatever star now builds a closure, and lists :D and :U type modifiers among the additions in 2011.09.

https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.says: Names WhateverCode as the type of the closures a star term builds, replacing Code:($), and HyperWhateverCode for the double-star form, so multiple dispatch can tell them from Whatever.

https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.where: Raku/old-design-docs commit 04840a3 (Pugs svn r27265), S12 among others
https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.says: Besides header clean-ups across the Synopses, adds a conjectural S12 section deriving Int:A, Int:U and Int:D from a type name to accept any, only undefined or only defined values.

https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.where: perl6-language mailing list, svn commit mail for r10804 (msg25795)
https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.says: Mails the S06 change that introduces MAIN: called only when the file is run directly, with arguments bound by signature, multi dispatch over candidates, and USAGE or a generated message on failure.

https://github.com/Raku/mu/commit/4a841a.where: Raku/mu (Pugs svn mirror) commit 4a841a8, svn.perl.org r10804, S06 and S02
https://github.com/Raku/mu/commit/4a841a.says: Commits the first definition of MAIN subs to S06, mapping command-line switches to named parameters, with multi MAIN candidates and a USAGE fallback, and credits Aaron Crane for a typo fix.

https://github.com/rakudo/rakudo/commit/.says: Adds rudimentary support for a MAIN sub as the program's entry point, which at this stage hands every command-line argument over as a positional.

https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.where: Raku/old-design-docs commit dc6f02a (Pugs svn r25122), S02
https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.says: Adds a sentence to S02 saying Perl handles Unicode text in NFG by default, treating each grapheme, diacritics and all, as a single character.

https://6guts.wordpress.com/2015/04/30/t.who: Jonathan Worthington, MoarVM and Rakudo developer
https://6guts.wordpress.com/2015/04/30/t.where: 6guts blog, This week: the big NFG switch on, and many fixes
https://6guts.wordpress.com/2015/04/30/t.says: Reports that since 24 April 2015 every string Rakudo handles on the MoarVM backend is grapheme-based, with an example whose chars count is 1 while its NFC codepoint count is 2.

https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.where: Raku/old-design-docs commit f431adc (Pugs svn r28881), S02
https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.says: Adds to S02 that decimal literals without an exponent are kept as Rat, with examples showing 1.23456 as a Rat and 6.02e23 as a Num.

https://github.com/rakudo/rakudo/commit/.says: Adds a 47-line first draft of the Rat rational-number type to Rakudo's Perl 6 setting.

https://github.com/rakudo/rakudo/commit/.who: Solomon Foster, Rakudo contributor, with Moritz Lenz
https://github.com/rakudo/rakudo/commit/.says: Makes dividing two Ints with / return a Rat and div return an Int, following the then-current S03, and adds mixed Rat and Int arithmetic.

https://github.com/Raku/mu/commit/a8389e.where: Pugs svn r83 (Raku/mu commit a8389eb), src/AST.hs
https://github.com/Raku/mu/commit/a8389e.says: Adds a Bool-to-Rat conversion to the VRat rational value type already defined in the Pugs interpreter's Haskell AST, thanking viirya.

https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.who: Jonathan Worthington, Rakudo and MoarVM developer
https://github.com/Raku/old-design-docs/.says: Adds a concurrency Synopsis written anew and called heretical, describing what Rakudo on the JVM already did plus planned work, with sections on schedulers, promises, channels and subscribables, for discussion.

https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.says: Answers Larry Wall's call for a new word for superposition by offering alternatives such as multivalue, opval, set, junction and junctive, formatted as one any() call.

https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.where: perl6-language mailing list, Re: [RFC] Perl6 HyperOperator List (msg11927)
https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.says: Dismisses the coined term flexprs as no clearer than superpositions and says he would rather use an ugly but clear name such as junctions, or junks for short.

https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.where: perl6-language mailing list, Re: [RFC] Perl6 HyperOperator List (msg12007)
https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.per.says: Accepts Larry Wall's suggested name junctions, recalling his electrical engineering days, and commits to using the word from then on.

Proposes keeping French quotes for qw lists and writing vector multiply with inward-pointing quotes around the operator, and >>*<< as a plain-ASCII spelling, with bit shifts requalified as +>> and ~>>.

https://github.com/Raku/mu/commit/088e2d.where: Raku/mu (Pugs svn mirror) commit 088e2dc, svn.perl.org r11969, S03
https://github.com/Raku/mu/commit/088e2d.says: Adds X to S03 as a fifth metaoperator that applies an operator to every pairing drawn from its lists, and as a cross-product operator by itself, with X~ and X* examples.

https://github.com/Raku/mu/commit/c76102.where: Raku/mu (Pugs svn mirror) commit c761027, svn.perl.org r13699, S03
https://github.com/Raku/mu/commit/c76102.says: Renames the zip operator from the yen sign to Z and makes plain X the list cross operator, formerly XX, so the old string-concatenating X becomes X~X.

https://github.com/Raku/mu/commit/18d314.where: Raku/mu (Pugs svn mirror) commit 18d3149, svn.perl.org r14586, S03
https://github.com/Raku/mu/commit/18d314.says: Adds the infix series operator (three dots) to S03, with a Fibonacci example and a rule that deduces arithmetic or geometric progressions when the right operand is the Whatever star.
